current_episode.title: Why we need to give credit to those who manage our payrolls

guest.bio_context: Jason Davenport spent 10 years in construction delivering in-house weekly payrolls before transitioning to business process outsourcing at CMG (later acquired by Logica, now CGI), where he became associate director and director. He gained international experience working across France, Netherlands, Belgium, India, Philippines, and America on shared service centers delivering payroll services across up to 127 countries. He served as non-executive director and board member of CIPP from 2012 to 2021, ran his own consultancy, and joined CIPP as CEO in July of the previous year. He is also a mentor in the UK government's Be the Business scheme supporting SME productivity.

pending_qa.q: What career progression routes does CIPP offer to payroll professionals?
pending_qa.r: CIPP offers chartered membership and career designations supporting progression from student and junior member levels through to full member based on experience, chartered member, and fellow status. This reflects the status and professionalism of individuals on their career journey, similar to other chartered institutes like those for accountants and engineers.

pending_qa.q: What are the challenges payroll teams face with software compliance and testing?
pending_qa.r: Employers must ensure their payroll software is properly tested and embedded with all legislation changes, as new tax regimes, national insurance bands, and operating limits require continuous updates. Jason Davenport emphasizes that even though payroll now relies on software rather than hand calculations, teams must continually test software to ensure it is working correctly and compliantly.

pending_qa.q: What international collaboration does CIPP engage in regarding payroll standards?
pending_qa.r: CIPP works with the American Payroll Association (Payroll Org), the Canadian National Payroll Institute, and organizations in South Africa and Australia. While each country has different tax systems, they share common challenges such as pension enrollment and ensuring individuals are secure in retirement, allowing for collaborative development of courses and standards.
